# The complete ssh(1) command line Focal builds, one case per block. These lines
# are the security boundary in its most readable form: everything a remote host
# receives is here, in this order, and nothing else. A diff in this file is a
# change to what Focal can run, so it is meant to be reviewed by reading.
#
# Shape: ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes [-i key] [-p port] -- <target> [sudo -n] <program> <args...>
#
# "--" appears exactly once, immediately before the target, so a destination
# that somehow began with "-" is still an operand rather than an option. It is
# deliberately absent before the remote command: ssh sends everything after the
# destination to the remote host verbatim, and a literal "--" there would be
# passed on as the program name.

# plain
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com uptime

# user in target
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- ops@example.com uptime

# identity file
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -i /home/focal/.ssh/id_ed25519 -- example.com uptime

# port
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -p 2222 -- example.com uptime

# identity file and port
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -i /home/focal/.ssh/id_ed25519 -p 2222 -- ops@example.com uptime

# ipv6 target
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- ops@[2001:db8::1] uptime

# sudo prefix
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com sudo -n uptime

# command arguments
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com systemctl show nginx.service

# sudo prefix with command arguments
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -i /home/focal/.ssh/id_ed25519 -p 2222 -- ops@example.com sudo -n systemctl show nginx.service

# Below: one block per exported factory, built against example.com with no
# options and no sudo, so that the part that differs between them is the remote
# command itself. Together they are the complete set of programs Focal can ask
# a host to run; a factory added without a block here fails the count check in
# TestBuildArgvMatchesGolden.
#
# The caller-supplied tokens in these lines are nginx.service (a
# vo.ServiceName), 30m and 1h (a vo.Duration) and 200 (a vo.LineLimit).
# Everything else is a string literal in commands.go.

# UptimeCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com uptime

# UnameCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com uname -a

# HostnameCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com hostname

# DateCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com date --iso-8601=seconds

# OSReleaseCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com cat /etc/os-release

# LSCPUCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com lscpu

# LoadAvgCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com cat /proc/loadavg

# FreeCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com free -b

# MemInfoCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com cat /proc/meminfo

# DFCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com df -PT

# LSBLKCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com lsblk -o NAME,TYPE,SIZE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS

# FindMntCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com findmnt

# IPAddrCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com ip -details addr show

# IPRouteCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com ip route show

# SocketStatsCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com ss -lntup

# ResolvConfCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com cat /etc/resolv.conf

# ProcessListCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com ps -eo pid,ppid,user,state,%cpu,%mem,etime,comm,args

# ServiceStatusCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com systemctl show nginx.service --no-pager --property=Id,Description,LoadState,ActiveState,SubState,MainPID,ExecMainStatus,Result

# LogsCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com journalctl -u nginx.service --since=-30m -n 200 --no-pager --output=short-iso

# KernelLogsCommand
ssh -n -T -o BatchMode=yes -- example.com journalctl -k --since=-1h -n 200 --no-pager --output=short-iso
